connections.title: Opening a connection
connections.para1: Hover over the thin strip on the left edge of the screen to open the connection panel. It shows "My Connections" — a private list only you can see — plus any shared lists you've been given access to.
connections.para2: Click a list to expand it, then click a connection to open it. The connection loads on the right side of the screen; the panel slides away automatically once you click elsewhere, so it never shrinks or resizes your session.
connections.para3: If a session disconnects unexpectedly, it will try to reconnect on its own. If it can't, you'll see a reconnect option.
connections.para4: You can have several connections open at once. When more than one is open, a row of tabs appears at the top so you can click between them. There's also a <1>Sessions</1> button in the top-right corner that always shows what's open, even if only one connection is active — click it to jump to a session or close one.
connections.para5: You can also switch with the keyboard: hold the <1>left</1> Ctrl and Alt keys together and press the <3>Left</3> or <5>Right</5> arrow to move to the previous or next session. Press <7>Up</7> instead (still holding Ctrl+Alt) to see a snapshot of every open session at once and click the one you want.

bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
bookmarks.para1: Bookmarks are plain links you want quick access to, shown alongside your connections. Click <1>+ Add</1> at the top of the bookmark list to add one.
bookmarks.para2: Most bookmarks are <1>direct</1> — they open in a new browser tab like any normal link. Some are marked <3>proxied</3>: these point to internal systems your browser can't reach directly, so the app fetches the page on your behalf. Proxied bookmarks work the same way to click, just behind the scenes they're reached differently.
bookmarks.para3: You can export your bookmarks to a file that Chrome, Firefox, or Edge can import directly (look for "Export for browser"), and import an existing browser bookmarks export the same way.

files.title: Copy, paste & files
files.paraClipboard1: Copying and pasting plain text works both ways, automatically, in every kind of session — RDP, SSH, and the rest. Copy something on your own computer and paste (Ctrl+V) into the session, or copy something inside the session and paste it into another app on your own computer afterward — the same Ctrl+V (or Cmd+V on a Mac) either way, nothing special to remember per session type.
files.paraClipboard2: Copying something inside the session usually reaches your own computer's clipboard within a second, ready to paste elsewhere. Occasionally, depending on your browser, it may take one more local key press to actually land — if a paste seems to be missing the latest thing you copied inside the session, just try it again.
files.para1: <0>To send a file into a session:</0> drag it from your own computer and drop it anywhere in the session window. You'll see a progress indicator while it uploads.
files.para2: On an <1>RDP</1> session, the file lands in a folder called "Guacamole Transfer" inside the remote desktop — open that folder to find it. On an <3>SSH</3> session, the app types the file's new path at your cursor once the upload finishes, ready to use in a command.
files.para3: <0>To bring a file back out</0> of an RDP session, drag it into that same "Guacamole Transfer" folder from inside the remote desktop. A small notice appears in the bottom-left of your screen once it's ready — click it to download.

recording.title: Recording a session
recording.para1: While connected, click <1>Record</1> near the top of the session window to start recording. The button turns red and shows a timer while recording is active — click it again to stop.
recording.para2: Some connections are set up to record automatically for compliance reasons; if so, you'll see a recording indicator without a way to turn it off for that particular connection.

sharing.title: Sharing a session live
sharing.para1: You can invite someone to watch or help with a session you have open, in real time — useful for training, troubleshooting together, or a second pair of eyes on something. Look for the <1>Share</1> button next to Record while a session is open.
sharing.para2: Add the person, then choose <1>View only</1> (they can watch but not type or click) or <3>Can control</3> (they can type and click too, the same as you). You can change this or remove someone at any time — removing someone ends their view immediately, and closing the session yourself ends it for everyone still watching, not just you.
sharing.para3: When you share a session, the other person gets a pop-up notification with a <1>Join</1> button right away — they don't need to go looking for it. If they'd rather check later, it also shows up under <4>Sessions → Shared with you</4>. Opening it joins the same live session you have open — you're both looking at (and possibly both controlling) the exact same thing at the same time. Being invited into a session doesn't give you any other access to that system beyond what's happening in that session.

demos.title: Demos
demos.para1: A demo is a small, curated set of connections and bookmarks someone has put together and shared with you specifically — for example, a demo environment for a particular product walkthrough. Switch to the<1> Demos</1> tab at the top of the screen to see any demos shared with you, or to create your own if you have something to curate.
demos.para2: Being given access to a demo only gives you the items in that demo — it doesn't give you any broader access to the systems those items happen to live on.

account.title: Your account
account.para1: If an administrator resets your password, you'll be asked to set a new one the next time you sign in before you can do anything else. You can also change your password at any time from your account.
account.para2: Two-factor authentication (an authenticator app code) is required to sign in. If you lose access to your authenticator, contact an administrator — they can reset your account so you can set it up again.
account.para3: You can switch the app's color theme from the theme picker in the header — <1>Signal (Dark)</1>, <3>Daylight</3>, <6>Midnight</6>, or <8>Comic</8>. This is a personal preference saved on this browser, not something an administrator sets for you.
account.para4: If more than one language is available, a language picker also appears in the header, next to the theme picker — this is a personal preference too, saved on this browser.
